transcript.content:
Based on my investigation, I've identified the root cause and the files that need modification.

**Root cause:** When the AWS SDK uses `STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` (aws-chunked content encoding), the request body received by LocalStack is the raw chunked payload (with chunk-size lines and `chunk-signature` extensions), as seen in the trace: `data: b'93;chunk-signature=...\r\n...'`. The `check_content_md5` function in `s3_listener.py` computes the MD5 over this raw chunked body instead of the decoded content, so it never matches the `Content-MD5` header (which is computed over the actual decoded object content), producing the `BadDigest` error.

**Files to modify:**

1. **`localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py`** — `check_content_md5()` must detect streaming/aws-chunked requests (the constants `CONTENT_SHA256_HEADER` / `STREAMING_HMAC_PAYLOAD` already exist here but are unused) and decode the chunked payload before computing the MD5. The `forward_request` path calls `check_content_md5(data, headers)` with the raw chunked bytes.

2. **`localstack/utils/http_utils.py`** — `parse_chunked_data()` currently uses regex `^([0-9a-zA-Z]+)\r\n.*` which only handles plain chunked transfer encoding. It cannot parse aws-chunked bodies where the size line contains extensions like `93;chunk-signature=...\r\n` (and it only handles `str`, while S3 passes `bytes`). It must be updated to support chunk extensions so the S3 listener can decode the payload correctly.
